input:
Draft one catalogue Pattern for the policy. Return only the JSON object. Do not add prose.

Policy:
Pay the bill. Keep a credit.

Use pattern_id exactly as listed. Include only the parameters that pattern declares, under those exact names. Omit every other field.

A parameter whose kind is attribute-key must be "ledger.bill.id".
A parameter whose kind is selector must be one of these event kinds:
- ledger.agent.pay_bill (the agent pays the bill)
- ledger.exchange.settled (the exchange records the bill's first settlement)
- ledger.exchange.payment (the exchange records another payment on an already settled bill)
- ledger.exchange.credit (the exchange records a credit that closes the bill)
A parameter whose kind is sequence-lookback-bound or count-threshold must be an integer.

Patterns:
- precedence.approval (precedence): A named Event never occurs unless a qualifying Event for the same Binding lies in its causal past.
  - binding_attribute (attribute-key): The Event attribute whose value names a Binding. Each Binding gets its own Slice and its own Verdict, which is what makes the property uncheckable by a local guardrail.
  - trigger (selector): Events that create the obligation. One obligation per matching Event per Binding.
  - requirement (selector): Events that discharge the obligation. A matching Event must lie in the trigger's causal past in every admissible linearization.
- provenance.taint (reachability): A named Event never occurs when an Event marking untrusted content for the same Binding lies in its causal past.
  - binding_attribute (attribute-key): The Event attribute whose value names a Binding. ADR-0016's differentiator is that the prohibited sequence is data-parametric: the question is not whether untrusted content was read anywhere, but whether it reached this recipient's and this workflow's action.
  - action (selector): Events whose provenance is constrained. One obligation per matching Event per Binding, and the selector the census keys on: an evidence set with taint markers and no action establishes nothing.
  - untrusted_content (selector): Events marking the ingestion of untrusted content. A matching Event falsifies the property when it lies in an action's causal past. It may match freely elsewhere in the Trace and usually does, which is why it is not the selector the census keys on.
- absence.after-until (absence): A named veto Event never occurs inside the open interval (after, until] for the same Binding.
  - binding_attribute (attribute-key): The Event attribute whose value names a Binding. Each Binding gets its own Slice and its own Verdict: the question is whether a veto reached this Binding's open interval, not whether a veto occurred anywhere.
  - after (selector): Events that open the interval. Present in evidence as a delimiter; contributing-tier witness suffices, as with CAT-1's trigger. Reported as the interval's opening count, not as the census key.
  - until (selector): Events that close the interval and raise the absence obligation. One obligation per matching Event per Binding, and the selector the census keys on: an evidence set full of vetoes and no until establishes nothing.
  - veto (selector): Events prohibited inside (after, until]. A matching Event falsifies the property when it lies in that open interval. It may match freely outside it and usually does, which is why it is not the selector the census keys on.
- aggregation.count-within (aggregation): At a trigger Event, the count of matching member Events inside a sequence lookback for the same Binding must stay strictly below a threshold.
  - binding_attribute (attribute-key): The Event attribute whose value names a Binding. Each Binding gets its own Slice and its own Verdict: the rate cap is per Binding, not a global count across principals.
  - trigger (selector): Events that raise the aggregation obligation (the assessment / privileged action). One obligation per matching Event per Binding, and the selector the census keys on: an evidence set full of members and no trigger establishes nothing.
  - member (selector): Events counted inside the sequence lookback. Their count is compared to threshold once the cold path holds a complete lookback. Members may match freely and must never be the census key — a clean under-threshold deployment would otherwise report as never exercised.
  - lookback (sequence-lookback-bound): How many sequence positions of causal evidence to include when counting members. Sequence positions, not wall-clock seconds/minutes/hours/days; Dogwood duration leaves are refused by Tier-1 (#174), not silently lowered.
  - threshold (count-threshold): Exclusive upper bound on the member count inside the lookback: complete lookback with count < threshold may settle Satisfy after cold Holds; count ≥ threshold Fails the guard (Authoritative Inconclusive in PR-1 until #20).
- existence.before-scope-close (existence): A named Event occurs at least once inside a Between Scope before that Scope closes, for the same Binding.
  - binding_attribute (attribute-key): The Event attribute whose value names a Binding. Each Binding gets its own Slice and its own Verdict.
  - open (selector): Events that open the Between Scope and raise the existence obligation. The census keys on this selector only — never on required alone, which would vacuous-pass a Trace full of compensations with no saga open.
  - required (selector): Events that must occur at least once inside (open, close]. Their presence discharges the obligation; their absence at a settled close is the Violate.
  - close (selector): Events that close the Between Scope. ADR-0025 licenses Satisfy only when the Scope closes without a bad prefix; retirement while still open pins structural Inconclusive rather than inventing a Satisfy.
